Thuma Mina

By: Diana Lucas | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Summary:
Thuma Mina is a call from the people of South Africa to the people of South Africa to show up for each other and carry each other. 

Hugh Masekela’s Thuma Mina was the message President Cyril Ramaphosa brought to his 2018 state of the nation address to South Africa’s Parliament. He was not only honouring the musician, who had passed away but using the song ‘Send Me’ to highlight – implore - South African citizens to stand up and take individual responsibility for the state of our nation.

Now, in the middle of the worst pandemic the world has seen in a century, Bra Hugh’s fellow musicians and artists have come together for a collaborative remix and remake of his haunting call.

Why? Well in the words of Zolani Mahola (ex-lead singer of Freshly Ground), who has taken part in this re make, this is an amazing sentiment and call to action for South Africans at this time. She speaks about the spirit of the message, a need to inspire and uplift. We all have a role to play in this country, however small.



Further information:
The song evokes the lyrics of a hugely popular traditional gospel chorus which highlights themes of self sacrifice, individual responsibility and the importance of personal change in mind sets. ‘And I heard the voice of the Lord saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” Then I said, “Here am I! Send me.”’ – Isaiah 6:8

For Bra Hugh who released Thuma Mina in 2002 as a recovering addict, the message was particularly poignant. But his vision was always one of South Africans uniting and helping each other through troubled times.

His nephew Selema Writes brings a new freestyle rap element to the arrangement.
‘Thuma Min,a when I listen I think of my uncle and the difficulties he had with his own life like drug addiction and once he got out of that and he didn’t do it alone he had help’ For Selema this need to make a positive influence on others and Bra Hugh’s own consciousness arising through the song (that I am not her just for my self and what is humanity without connection?) is the real guts of this call to action.

A host of South Africa’s finest and most celebrated producers, musical directors and musicians showed up – including Abigail Kubeka, Vusi Mahlasela, Thandiswe Mazwai, Zolani Mahola and J’Something. But also featuring in the music video are heroes who are showing up for each other at this stressful time. Individuals and initiatives stepping up and helping fellow South Africans.

Like Mshengu, a musician who through his culture foundation is organising and distributing food parcels to disadvantaged people.

Dominic Shillie who helps about 1 500 kids from his community, feeding, cooking and donating clothes.

Singer Thembi Tshabalala, who teaches extra-mural activities to kids from the informal settlements, but also provides a hot meal first.

Jean Bwasa and his wife Nicole, who look after the asylum-seekers and migrants that have also lost their job due to Covid-19

This video was the brainchild of Robbie Brozin (founder of Nando’s) to showcase and inspire ways for individuals to get involved, send people to the cause, igniting action to help one another. It was filmed at Constitutional Hill, in Zolano’s words “breathing new life into our history”.

With the music video and background action of the filming we will weave together interviews with the artists and friends of Hugh Masekela who see the need now for this call to action. We will feature some of the individuals who are helping their communities in different ways. And talk to Robbie Brozin on why he decided on this platform to take action and reach out to fellow South Africans.

Script:


UP SOUND MAC I want to Be there…..

V/O
When President Cyril Ramaphosa quoted the late Hugh Masekela’s song Thuma Mina, Send Me at the State of the Nation address in 2018, he was looking to South Africans to step up, lend a hand.

Link
Now during one of the centuries worst pandemic, Bra Hughes Fellow musicians and artists have joined forces for a collaborative remix of Thuma Mina…a call to action for South Africans to play a role however small

V/O
Singer, songwriter, Zolani Mahola is part of this re mix.

Zolani Mahola
Thuma Miena what an amazing sentiment send me I volunteer I will be there because I am part of the society I want to be there for my people.

V/O
Originally released in 2002 Thuma Mina was particularly personal for Ba Hugh, a recovering addict His nephew Selema Writes, who brings a free style rap element to the song, remembers

Selema Writes
I think of my uncle and I think about the difficulties he has had with his own life he was changing as an individual his spirit was changing he was realising I’m not just this guy who plays this amazing trumpet, this is humanity and what is humanity without connection and that’s how I look at the song it was a call for us to forget about our egos and to stretch out a hand to the next fellow sister brother and ask them is what I can do for you I am here for you.

V/O
Thuma Mina – The People Version is a collaboration between Constitution Hill, the Hugh Masekela Foundation and Flame Studios. Their aim to mobilise the people of South Africa into action.

Lwando: We thought its time to reinvigorate the idea of the constitution and its values in the peoples minds and the Thuma Mina song became a collision of those goals for all of us

V/O
Lwando Xaso is part of the Constitution Hill Trust.

Lwando Xaso
Constitution Hill Trust 

So we the people are the first three words to the SA constitution they said those words in 1955 when they drafted the Freedom Charter at a time of great division they didn’t come together and say we the oppressed people, we the black people, we the women of SA it as simply we the people of SA we see that as a rallying cry and a call for people to come together because the only time that any achievements and challenges have been over come in SA is when we have done it as We the People as a collective so we want to start that movement under that umbrella We the people.

V/O
And the people came to Constitutional Hill to take part. The Legendary Abigal Kubeka. who grew up with Hugh was there.

Abigal Kubeka
Abigail You know you sometimes forget the strength you have in you, you undermine yourself God couldn’t have made you without strength, just try and find out about that you got it in you stand up think.

Link: So besides the celebrities and the artists who are featured in this video there are also are ordinary South African’s that are feeding communities helping out wherever they can and doing their bit.

V/O
People like Dominic Shillie, cooking for and feeding the kids in his community

Dominic: What COVID did for us was expose what had been going down people are really suffering because I started with 50 kids and now I am serving up to a 1000.

V/O
And Jean Bwasa who focus’s on migrants who have had very little help during this time

HM and Mama Afrika was in the Congo during the apartheid time so, that’s where they have to learn their music so for me Thuma Mina was speaks to my heart I was sent in the same way Thuma Mina want s every individual human being to have a purpose in this life.

V/O
And providing the back up for these volunteers is the NPO, The Angel Network. They are assisting 150 000 desperate people. Their warehouse is Glynne Wolman’s garage

Glynne: As Bra Hugh says he says send me and I think that’s how the Angel Network started its about send me… ordinary people doing extra ordinary things its just mobilising the troops saying lend a hand show some support, kindness make a difference remember people who need help and help..

V/O
Thuma Mina – The Peoples Version is mot just a re make of a song but a movement with a vision to grow … It is time for the people to take the lead.

Zolani
II hope that a lot of younger people who might not know Hughes work I hope they take it on with the spirit that it was meant. The spirit that says you part of this country //// you have a role to play in making it the country we want to be
